assessment_summary: The proof introduces a false claim at line 0039, stating that P - C = {x : Ax <= b} (which is equivalent to saying P - C = P). The justification for this claim follows in line 0040, which relies on a flawed algebraic manipulation: subtracting the inequality Ac <= 0 from Ax <= b to conclude that Ax - Ac <= b - 0. In reality, since Ac <= 0, we have -Ac >= 0, so Ax - Ac is Ax plus a non-negative quantity, which can exceed b. This invalidates the construction of X.
counterexample: Let P = [0, \infty). Then A = -1, b = 0. The recession cone C = [0, \infty). Let x = 0 \in P and c = 1 \in C. Then x - c = -1. Evaluating A(x - c) gives -1(-1) = 1, which is not <= 0, so x - c \notin P. Thus P - C is not equal to {x : Ax <= b}.
